title: Tokyo World Championships: Team Rosters Revealed
text:
Ireland Announces 27-Athlete Team for World Athletics Championships Tokyo 2025 Ireland’s Athletics ireland has named a provisional team of 27 athletes set to compete at the World Championships in Tokyo, Japan, from September 13-21, 2025. The squad features a compelling mix of seasoned veterans and rising stars, poised to challenge on the global stage.
Key Athletes Headline Provisional Roster
The team boasts several athletes with recent international success. sarah Healy ,a European Indoor gold medalist in the 3000m from March 2024,will race the 1500m,marking her third appearance at the World Championships. Mark English , fresh off a bronze medal in the 800m at the European Championships in the Netherlands, has also been selected. English recently shattered his own Irish record in the 800m, clocking a time of 1:43.37 in Budapest on August 12, 2024.
O’Connor and Mawdsley Aim for Continued Success
Kate O’Connor will compete in the heptathlon, continuing her impressive trajectory in the multi-event discipline. Sharlene Mawdsley , a versatile athlete, is entered in the 400m and both the mixed and women’s 4x400m relays. Also included is Nicola Tuthill , who recently improved her personal best and Irish U-23 record to 71.75m in the hammer throw, having recently improved her personal best and Irish U-23 record to 71.75m. Marathon runners Hiko Tonosa , Peter Lynch , and Fionnuala McCormack were previously selected for the championships back in May.
Adeleke Withdraws Due to Injury
The team will, though, be without Rhasidat Adeleke , who confirmed last week that she will not be traveling to Tokyo.The 22-year-old, who qualified in both the 200m and 400m, struggled to regain peak form throughout the summer.”I am unable to complete the season and will be taking the rest of the year off to recover,” Adeleke stated in a post on Instagram.
Full Team Roster
Sarah Healy (1500m) Sophie O’Sullivan (1500m) Mark English (800m) Sarah Lavin (100m hurdles) Sharlene Mawdsley (400m, mixed 4x400m, women’s 4x400m) Cian McPhillips (800m) Cathal Doyle (1500m) Andrew Coscoran (1500m, 5000m) Kate O’Connor (heptathlon) Nicola Tuthill (hammer throw) Brian Fay (5000m) David Kenny (20km race walk) Oisin Lane (35km race walk) Eric Favors (shot put) Fionnuala McCormack (marathon) Hiko Tonosa (marathon) Peter Lynch (marathon) Sophie Becker (mixed 4x400m, women’s 4x400m) Rachel McCann (mixed 4x400m, women’s 4x400m) jack Raftery (mixed 4x400m) Conor Kelly (mixed 4x400m) Cillín Greene (mixed 4x400m) cliodhna Manning (women’s 4x400m) Michelle Duggan (women’s 4x400m) Jenna Breen (women’s 4x400m) Erin Friel (non-travelling reserve, women’s 4x400m) Ciaran Carthy (non-travelling reserve, mixed 4x400m) The Irish team represents a significant investment in athletic talent and signals a strong commitment to competing at the highest level of international track and field.
